pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Mycosphaerella coffeicola (brown eye spot of coffee)

type_of_disease.quote: Spores of the fungus form in the grey centres

affected_parts.quote: Small brown spots occur on the leaves... On the berries, the infections are smaller than on leaves, less than 5 mm wide... in severe cases, stem dieback

summary.value: Small brown spots on leaves with light brown or grey centres surrounded by dark brown rings and yellow margins, growing up to 15 mm diameter. Smaller irregular brown spots on berries, less than 5 mm wide.
summary.quote: Small brown spots occur on the leaves, more obvious on the upper surface... The spots can grow up to 15 mm diameter; they have light brown or sometimes light grey centres, surrounded by a wide, dark brown ring, and a yellow margin... On the berries, the infections are smaller than on leaves, less than 5 mm wide, but sometimes they cover the whole berry

diagnostic_features.value: Circular brown spots mostly 5-10 mm with bright grey centres and yellow haloes; characteristic appearance with light brown or grey centers, dark brown outer ring, and yellow margins
diagnostic_features.quote: Circular brown spots, mostly 5-10 mm, with bright grey centres and yellow haloes, typical of brown-eye leaf spot... Look for the characteristic spots on the leaves with light brown (sometimes grey) centres, brown outside, surrounded by yellow margins

look_alikes.quote: Often, other fungi invade the berries following infections of Cercospora. The fungus, Colletotrichum gloeosporiodes is commonly present.

conflicts.note: Cercospora coffeicola is the asexual (anamorph) form; Mycosphaerella coffeicola is the sexual (teleomorph) form used by CABI as the primary name. No taxonomy validation data was provided to confirm current accepted name.
